newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel denies violating economic accord with PLO.
newsitem.headline: Israel denies violating economic accord with PLO.

text.p: Israel denied Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's charges that it had violated an economic accord with the PLO, saying it would demand its own changes in response to his demand to rewrite the agreement.

"Israel did not violate the agreement but if the Palestinians want to change the agreement Israel will also ask to introduce changes and it's not certain the Palestinians will want these proposed changes," a government official said.
The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, did not elaborate on changes Israel might seek.
Arafat told a Paris World Bank donors' meeting on the West Bank and Gaza that Israel had violated its 1994 economic agreement with the PLO.
He said the autonomous Palestinian areas were losing $7 million a day because of Israel's decision to close them off last February after bomb attacks by Moslem fundamentalists.

Arafat urged a revised accord which must force Israel to lift restrictions and quotas on direct imports by the Palestinians, transfer sales tax revenue collected by the Israeli treasury and recognise Palestinian technical standards.
The Israeli official said: "It should be remembered that Israel, within the framework of the agreement, has to date transferred $700 million to the Palestinians".
